title: Enhancing Persona Following at Decoding Time via Dynamic Importance Estimation for Role-Playing Agents
claim: A two-stage pipeline estimates context-dependent attribute importance, then uses it to weight rewards that steer decoding toward persona-consistent outputs.
layout: 3 columns, left-to-right: inputs, two module panels, output distribution; math in boxes
description: A left-to-right system diagram. The left dashed panel holds the full prompt T, split into three stacked parts: a Harry Potter profile card (name, style, personality, character), a scenario-context chat bubble exchange ("Avada Kedavra!" / "Expecto Patronum!"), and a query bubble. A blue arrow leads into panel (a), Persona Importance Estimation. There, persona attributes (Style, Personality, Character) pass through an LLM π_θ, and the entropy difference H(Y|P) − H(Y|P_i) gives the importance I_i. A green arrow leads into panel (b), Persona-Guided Inference-Time Alignment. There, two bar charts (unconstrained vs. persona-constrained) feed per-attribute rewards r_i, drawn as a gift-box icon. Both panels feed an orange R_norm formula box. That box points to a final bar chart of next-token probabilities p_r. Dashed callouts contrast a plain persona-prompt output with the PDD output, which has a green check and highlighted words. Colors are pastel blue, green and orange.
caption: Overview of the proposed PDD. Given a full prompt T including character profile P, scenario context C and a query x, PDD first dynamically estimates persona importance Ii for each persona attribute wi. Then we compute persona-guided rewards ri(T, y<t) by measuring the divergence between persona-constrained and unconstrained probability distributions. These individual rewards are then integrated into a normalized reward signal Rnorm, which emphasizes more important attributes through adaptive weighting. Finally, the aligned policy pr can be derived through reward maximization, thereby generating persona following responses.
abstract: The utility of Role-Playing Language Agents in sociological research is growing alongside the adoption of Large Language Models. For realism in social simulation, these agents must adhere to their personas defined by character profiles, yet existing strategies-static prompt engineering or costly fine-tuning-fail to adapt personas to dynamic scenarios. Psychological theories, such as the Cognitive-Affective Personality Systems, provide a crucial explanation for this failure: a persona's influence on behavior is not static but varies with the scenarios. This context-dependence highlights the critical need for adaptive persona management. To address this gap, we propose a novel, theory-driven method that dynamically estimates context-dependent persona importance and integrates it into weighted reward-guided decoding, enabling inference-time persona following. Specifically, we introduce the Persona Dynamic Decoding (PDD) framework, which consists of two key components: (1) Persona Importance Estimation (PIE) module, which dynamically quantifies the contextual importance of persona attributes without requiring ground-truth supervision; and (2) Persona-Guided Inference-Time Alignment (PIA) paradigm, which leverages these importance scores to construct weighted multi-objective rewards and modulate generation probabilities during inference. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method in utterance consistency and behavioral fidelity.
